history: Tianjin means 'the Emperor's ferry'. In 1404 Emperor Zhu Di named and fortified it — the only Chinese city with an exact recorded founding date. Opened as a treaty port in 1860, nine foreign concessions left it a showcase of international architecture; the Five Great Avenues are called a world architecture expo. Crosstalk comedy, Clay Figure Zhang and Yangliuqing New Year prints make it the home of Chinese folk performing arts. Today it is northern China's shipping hub — Tianjin Port is among the world's ten largest.
importance: Municipality · Northern China's largest port city
foods: Founded in 1858, the finest of Tianjin's 'three treasures' — 18-pleat dumplings with juicy filling.
Guifaxian stuffed dough twists: crispy, sweet and they never go soft.
Glutinous-rice fried cakes with red-bean paste — crispy outside, tender inside. One of the three treasures.
Mung-bean crepes with crispy fritters — the breakfast faith of Tianjin people.
Mung-bean crepe strips in savory gravy — 'Gabacai', a classic Tianjin morning dish.
Whole carp fried with scales until bone-crisp, splashing with sweet-and-sour sauce.
The traditional 'Eight Great Bowls' banquet — humble ingredients, masterful cooking.
Millet porridge topped with sesame paste — sip it around the rim of the bowl, the proper way.
Braised gluten in rich savory gravy — a homestyle rice companion.
Xiaobao chestnuts, sweet and starchy — the smell of autumn and winter streets.
scenes: A Ferris wheel built on a bridge — one full turn shows both banks of the Haihe.
An expo of 2,000+ European-style villas; a horse carriage carries you back a century.
